archetype.name: Playoff Team (5-on-5 driven)
archetype.definition: Ottawa wins the even-strength chance battle and has a Selke-and-Hart-calibre top of the lineup in Stützle, but its standing rests on a hot starting goalie while one of the league's worst power plays drags on it.

report.headline: Good 5-on-5 team hiding a broken power play behind Ullmark's hot start
report.take:
Ottawa is 11-6-1 through 18 games, fourth in a crowded Atlantic behind Boston, Montreal and Tampa, on a 105-point pace. The Teams tab is cooler on them at 15th of 32, and that gap is the story. At 5-on-5 this is a good team. Its 52.9 xGF % ranks 9th, it has the 8th-fewest goals allowed per game, and last season's 55.6 xGF % says the even-strength process isn't new. The shot attempts are only about even (49 CF %) and the shot volume is thin at 25.7 a game, 25th in the league. The Senators are winning on chance quality, not on possession.

The engine is Tim Stützle. He has 23 points, sits 7th of 233 on the centers tab and owns a 59% expected-goals share in nearly 22 minutes a night. Drake Batherson (9 goals, 9th among right wings) is the other finisher, and Claude Giroux and Fabian Zetterlund drive play on the second layer. Zetterlund's 63.2 xGF % has produced only 2 goals on 39 shots, so he is one of the few forwards due for more, not less. In net, Linus Ullmark has been elite: .945, 8.3 goals saved above expected, 5th on the goalies tab.

Two things the record hides cut in opposite directions. The power play is converting 13.2%, 31st, more than nine points under the league average, after running at 24% last season. That is almost certainly not who this team is, and it is real upside. The other is the crease. The team's 5-on-5 PDO of 102.7 and a Pts vs Goal Diff of +1.7 (6th) show a record running slightly ahead of a modest +4 goal differential. Behind Ullmark the goaltending has been poor. Samuel Ersson is at .889, and the listed pair's combined .916 sits well above the team-wide .901, so the remaining starts went badly too. Team GSAx is just 0.4, 18th. This franchise has lived through goaltending swings before: +23.7 GSAx two years ago, -24 last year.

The direction depends on which of those normalizes first. If the power play climbs back toward its usual level before Ullmark's save percentage falls to earth, Ottawa is a comfortable playoff team. If it happens the other way round, the last 10 games are the warning: 5-4-1, 3.4 goals allowed a game, and blowout losses to San Jose and Anaheim. That looks like a bubble team.

strengths.title: Wins the 5-on-5 chance battle
strengths.body: Ottawa's 52.9 xGF % ranks 9th and sits clearly above the league's 50, even though its raw attempt share is slightly under even. The Senators generate better looks than they give up, and the top forwards (Stützle, Batherson, Giroux, Zetterlund) all run expected-goals shares in the mid-50s or better. Last season's 55.6 shows the process is durable rather than an 18-game blip.

strengths.title: Stützle and Batherson carry the offense
strengths.body: Stützle's 23 points and 7th-of-233 tab rank make him a genuine first-line driver, and Batherson's 9 goals rank him 9th among right wings. The forward group grades B+ largely on their backs, with real depth in two-way play behind them. The finishing (12.1% team shooting, barely above the league's 11.6%) isn't inflated, so the scoring should hold.

strengths.title: Ullmark is stealing games
strengths.body: In his 8 starts Ullmark has a .945 save % and 8.3 goals saved above expected, 5th on the goalies tab. That is the biggest single reason the team allows only 3 goals a game despite a leaky penalty kill. Elite form is real value, but a .945 is not a level any goalie holds over a season.

concerns.title: Power play near the bottom
concerns.body: At 13.2% the power play ranks 31st, 9.3 points under the league average, with a penalty kill 22nd behind it. Special teams are erasing much of the 5-on-5 edge. Last season's 24% conversion with largely the same core says this should improve, but until it does, Ottawa is giving back goals every week.

concerns.title: Goaltending beyond Ullmark
concerns.body: Ersson's .889 and -1.4 GSAx are well below Ullmark's level. The team-wide .901 trails the listed pair's .916, which means the other starts were worse still. As a whole, the crease is only 18th in GSAx and grades C+. With a 102.7 PDO, any cooling from Ullmark or a larger share of starts for the backups exposes the shaky depth quickly.

concerns.title: Low shot volume, wingers get loose
concerns.body: Ottawa takes 25.7 shots a game, 25th, so it relies on quality over quantity. At the other end, opposing wingers score well above their norms: Ottawa ranks 26th, and wingers account for 45.8% of the points it allows against a league share of 38%. Lately the defense has leaked more, with 3.4 goals allowed a game over the last 10.

trend.note: A 9-6 October gave way to a choppier stretch. The last 10 went 5-4-1 with several lopsided losses, but the last five (3-1-1, including tight wins over Buffalo and Utah) steadied the ship at roughly the season's level.

weekAhead.headline: Two home games bracketing Colorado, the week's real test
weekAhead.body:
The week opens at home against Washington, a 9-6 team whose underlying 54% xGF share is better than Ottawa's. Its goaltending, though, grades D+ with an .886 save %, and its defense lets wingers run up points (28th). That plays to Batherson, Giroux and Amadio. Colorado comes to Ottawa next with the 3rd-best offense, 30.6 shots a game and an A forward group. Its goalies sit 27th in GSAx and its record lags its +0.89 goal differential, so the Avalanche are better than their 10-6-2.

The week closes in Pittsburgh. At 6-10-2 the Penguins look soft, but they win the attempt battle (53 CF %, 6th) and own one of the unluckiest records in the league. Their goaltending is the weakness: .876, 28th. Ottawa should expect to win the Washington and Pittsburgh games and must survive Colorado's volume. Splitting the starts sensibly between Ullmark and the backups decides how the three nights go.

keyMatchups.title: Ottawa's wingers vs leaky Capitals
keyMatchups.body: Washington allows wingers far more than they usually produce, ranking 28th, and its team save % is 20th. Batherson's finishing and Giroux's play-driving should find room. It's a game where Ottawa's chance quality should turn into goals.

keyMatchups.title: Stützle against Colorado's center leak
keyMatchups.body: Colorado's defense gives centers the most excess points of the three opponents (28th), so Stützle and Pinto have the matchup to exploit. The flip side is the Avalanche putting 30.6 shots a night on a team that only manages 25.7 itself. If Ottawa's backup starts this one, it is likely a loss.

keyMatchups.title: Pittsburgh's crease, not its record
keyMatchups.body: The Penguins' .876 save % ranks 28th and their defense gives forwards more than almost anyone (28th). Their 53 CF % means they will have the puck plenty, though, so this is not a free two points on the road.

weekAhead.watch: Who starts against Colorado. Ullmark in that game keeps the week on track; anyone else invites the kind of blowout Ottawa has already absorbed twice.

restOfSeason.body:
The 105-point pace leans on a .945 starter and a slightly favorable Pts vs Goal Diff, and both should fade. Expect Ullmark's save % to drift down and the backup starts to keep costing games. Against that, a 31st-ranked power play is the most obvious positive regression on the sheet: this group converted at 24% a year ago and has a legitimate first unit. The 5-on-5 chance share is the durable piece, and Sanderson has appeared in only 10 of the 18 games while scoring at a near point-a-game rate. A fuller blueline should help the 5-on-5 numbers too.

Net, Ottawa looks like a mid-to-high 90s points team, in the playoff race but not running away with a division where three teams are ahead of it. That fits last season's 99 points and better process numbers. The ceiling rises if the power play recovers to the league average while Ullmark stays merely good. The floor is a bubble finish if the crease behind him keeps leaking.

confidence.note: 18 games: the 5-on-5 process has a track record, but the goaltending and power-play numbers are small, volatile samples.
